questions.question: In the middle of which century did the Arab traveler Sulaiman visit India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**9th.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sulaiman**, also known as **Sulaiman al-Tajir**, visited India in the **9th century.**
 
• He was an Arab traveler and merchant who wrote about his travels in a book called **"Kitab al-Masalik wa al-Mamalik"** (Book of Roads and Kingdoms).
 
• Sulaiman's account of his journey provides valuable information about the **political, social, and economic** conditions of India during that time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• The **15th century** was a significant period in Indian history, marked by the rise of the** Vijayanagara Empire** and the arrival of the **Portuguese.**
 
• The **11th century** saw the reign of **King Rajendra Chola**, who expanded the Chola Empire through conquest and trade.
 
• The **6th century **was a time of political and social upheaval in India, with the **decline of the Gupta Empire** and the emergence of regional kingdoms.

questions.question: The correct order of electron affinity of halogens is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **electron affinity** of halogens is the energy change that occurs when an** electron is added** to a neutral atom to form a **negative ion.**
 
• The correct order of electron affinity of halogens is** I **
 
• This is because as we move down the group, the **atomic radius increases,** and the distance between the nucleus and the valence electrons **increases**, leading to a **decrease** in the attraction between the nucleus and the added electron.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The chemical element **iodine** has the atomic number** 53 **and the symbol **I.**

 
 
• The **heaviest stable** halogen, it is a **semi-lustrous, non-metallic solid** at ordinary circumstances.
 
 
 
• At normal temperature, **bromine** is a naturally occurring **liquid element**.
 
 
• It **dissolves in water** and has a** brownish-red color** and bleach-like smell.
 
 
 
• The chemical element **fluorine** has an atomic number of **nine** and the symbol **F.**
 
 
• Fluorine is a gas at room temperature and is categorized as a **halogen.**
 
 
 
• The chemical element **chlorine **has the atomic number **17 **and the symbol **Cl**.
 
 
• The** second-lightest** of the halogens, it is found on the periodic table between** fluorine and bromine,** with most of its properties falling in the middle of the two.

questions.question: The government is bound to ensure observance of social welfare and labour laws enacted to secure for workmen a life compatible with human dignity, under ________ of the Indian Constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 21.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 21** of the Indian Constitution guarantees the **right to life and personal liberty**, which includes the right to live with dignity. 
 
• The government is responsible for ensuring the **protection of fundamental rights **and the **welfare of its citizens**, especially those who are vulnerable and marginalized.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 17** of the Indian Constitution abolishes the practice of** untouchability** and prohibits its **enforcement** in any form. 
 
• **Article 15 **prohibits discrimination on the grounds of **religion, race, caste, sex,** or place of birth.
 
 
• This article is important for ensuring **social justice and equality.**
 
 
 
• **Article 19** protects the **freedom of speech and expression,** the** right to assemble peaceably** and without arms, the right to form associations or unions, and the right to move freely throughout the** territory of India.**

questions.question: Which great leader died due to his injuries in the Anti-Simon Commission Protest of 1928?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lala Lajpat Rai.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai** was a prominent **Indian freedom fighter** and leader of the** Indian National Congress.**
 
• He was a vocal opponent of **British rule in India** and played a key role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• In **1928**, he led a protest against the **Simon Commission**, a British government initiative to review the Indian constitution, which was seen as an attempt to prolong **British rule.**
 
• During the protest, Lala Lajpat Rai was brutally beaten by the** police** and sustained **serious injuries.**
 
• He **died **a few weeks later.
 
• His death sparked widespread outrage and further fuelled the** Indian independence movement.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lala Hardayal **was another Indian freedom fighter and founder of the** Ghadar Party,** which was dedicated to the overthrow of British rule in India.

 
 
• He died **March 4, 1939.**
 
 
 
• **Bhagat Singh** was a **revolutionary socialist** who played a key role in the Indian independence movement.
 
 
• He was **executed** by the British government in **1931.**
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** was a prominent **Indian nationalist and social reformer** who advocated for **Indian self-rule **and played a key role in the Indian National Congress.
 
 
• He died in **1920.**

questions.question: The estimation of the poverty line in India is based on the survey conducted by which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Statistical Office (NSO).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The National Statistical Office (NSO)** conducts a survey on household consumption expenditure every **five years** to estimate the **poverty line** in India.
 
• The **poverty line** is defined as the **minimum level of income** required to meet the basic needs of an individual.
 
• The survey collects data on various parameters such as** food and non-food consumption, health and education expenditure**, and** housing conditions.**
 
• The poverty line is calculated based on the cost of a **minimum food basket **plus** expenditure** on non-food items.
 
• The poverty line is used to identify households that are eligible for various welfare schemes such as** food subsidies, rural employment guarantee schemes, and housing programs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Finance:**

 
 
• It is responsible for preparing the** Union Budget of India** and managing the country's public finances.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**:
 
 
• It is the central bank of India and is responsible for regulating the **country's monetary policy** and managing its **foreign exchange reserves.**
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Rural Development:****​ **
 
 
• **​**It is responsible for implementing various rural development programs such as the** Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme, Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, **and **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan.**
 
 
 
• **The National Sample Survey Office** (NSSO) is a wing of the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme** Implementation and is responsible for conducting l**arge-scale sample surveys** in diverse fields on an All India basis.

questions.question: According to the Indian Minerals Yearbook 2020, which state in India has the highest share of limestone production?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajasthan** has the highest share of **limestone production** in India, accounting for about **29%** of the total production in the country.
 
• With **27% **of the total resources, **Karnataka **is the most **resource-rich state**, followed by **Rajasthan** and **Andhra Pradesh (12% each), Gujarat (10%), and Meghalaya (9%).**
 
• **Limestone** is a **sedimentary rock** composed mainly of **calcium carbonate** and is used in various industries, including **cement, steel, and chemicals**.
 
• The two minerals that make up limestone's majority are **aragonite and calcite**, which are distinct crystal forms of **CaCO₃.**
 
• When these minerals separate from water that has dissolved calcium, limestone is created. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telangana** has only a small share of about **1%** of the total production.
 
• **Chhattisgarh** is the** second-largest producer** of limestone in India.
 
 
• It is accounting for about** 17%** of the total production.
 
 
 
• **Madhya Pradesh** is also a significant producer of limestone.
 
 
• It has a share of about **13% **of the total production.

questions.question: The era of five-year plans began in India with the establishment of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Planning Commission. **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Planning Commission** was established in** 1950 **to formulate and implement **economic plans** and policies for the country.
 
• It was responsible for creating **five-year plans **for the development of various sectors in India.
 
• The first five-year plan was launched in **1951** and focused on **agriculture, irrigation, power, and transport. **
 
• Subsequent plans addressed issues such as **poverty alleviation, industrialization, and education.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Planning Commission was replaced by the** NITI Aayog in 2015**.

 
 
• The new organization is responsible for providing **strategic and technical advice** to the government on various policy matters.
 
 
 
• The **Parliament** is the supreme legislative body of India, consisting of the** President, the Rajya Sabha** (Council of States), and the **Lok Sabha** (House of the People).
 
 
• It is responsible for** enacting laws **and overseeing the functioning of the government.
 
 
 
• The** Finance Commission** is a constitutional body that is responsible for recommending the distribution of **tax revenues** between the central and state governments.
 
 
• It is also responsible for recommending measures to improve the** financial position** of the states.

questions.question: Which of the following principles was added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: The State shall provide free and compulsory education
To organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines
To protect and improve the environment and to safeguard forests and wildlife
Reservation of SC's and ST's in services

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To protect and improve the environment and to safeguard forests and wildlife.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42nd Constitutional Amendment** was passed in **1976** during the** emergency period** in India.
 
• It was a controversial amendment as it granted more powers to the **central government** and curtailed the powers of the state governments.
 
• The amendment added several new principles to the Indian Constitution, including the** protection and improvement **of the environment.
 
• This principle is important as India is a country with **diverse ecological systems and wildlife**, and **environmental degradation **has become a major issue in recent years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The State shall provide free and compulsory education - which was added by the **86th Constitutional Amendment in 2002**.

 
 
• This amendment made **education** a** fundamental right** for children aged **6-14 years.**
 
 
 
• Organizing agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines - is a **directive principle of state policy** (DPSP) in the Indian Constitution.
 
 
• DPSPs are **non-justiciable principles** that the state is expected to follow but cannot be enforced by courts.
 
 
 
• Reservation of SCs and STs in services - is a provision made in the Indian Constitution to provide **affirmative action** to historically marginalized communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The periodic growth and drop in seawater level is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**tide.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tides** are the **periodic rise and fall **of sea water levels caused by the **gravitational pull **of the** moon and the sun.**
 
• The cycle of **high tides and low tides** occurs **twice a day,** with a period of about **12 hours** and **25 minutes.**
 
• Tides are important for** navigation, fishing**, and other** marine activities.**
 
• They also play a role in shaping **coastlines and ecosystems.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Waves** are the movement of energy through the water caused by **wind, earthquakes, or other disturbances.**

 
 
• They can be** large or small **and travel long distances.
 
 
 
• **Sea currents** are the **continuous flow of water** in the ocean caused by differences in **temperature, salinity, and wind patterns**.
 
 
• They can be surface currents or deep currents and have a significant impact on** climate and marine life.**
 
 
 
• A brief influx of water onto ordinarily dry terrain is known as **flooding**.
 
 
• **Rain, snow, storm surges, coastal storms, river overflows**, and **dam failure** can all cause flooding.
 
• Floods are **not** always safe.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: In which of the following years did the East India Company abolish the diarchy system of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1772.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• East India Company **abolished** the **diarchy system of Bengal** in **1772.**
 
• The Diarchy system refers to the** dual system of administration **where the British East India Company **shared power** with the** Nawabs of Bengal.**
 
• The diarchy system was abolished due to various reasons, including the Company's desire for** more direct control over Bengal **and the **inefficiency and corruption** of the system.
 
• The Company's officials believed that the system was hindering their efforts to** extract maximum revenue **from Bengal.
 
• After the abolition of the diarchy system, the Company took direct control over **Bengal's administration** and introduced various reforms to improve the **efficiency and transparency **of the system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The system was introduced in **1765 **through the **Treaty of Allahabad **signed between the **Company and the Mughal Emperor.**
 
• The diarchy system gave the Company control over **revenue collection and civil administration**, while the Nawabs retained control over the** police and criminal justice system.**
 
• **Year 1757** is the year when the** Battle of Plassey** took place and the Company gained control over Bengal.

questions.question: In India, which Ministry issues the coins of all denominations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Ministry of Finance.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Finance** is responsible for issuing **coins of all denominations** in India.
 
• The coins are minted by the government-owned **Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India Limited** (SPMCIL) and its four mints located in **Mumbai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, and Noida.**
 
• The coins are issued on behalf of the **Reserve Bank of India** (RBI), which is the country's **central bank.**
 
• The coins are **legal tender** and can be used for** transactions **in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Ministry of External Affairs** is responsible for** India's foreign policy, diplomatic relations** with other countries, and** international trade and cooperation.**

 
 
• It was formed on** 2 September 1946.**
 
 
 
• The** Ministry of Home Affairs** is responsible for maintaining** internal security, law and order, disaster management**, and **border management**.
 
 
• It was formed on **15 August 1947.**
 
 
 
• The** Ministry of Mines** is responsible for the development and regulation of the mining sector, including **exploration, production, and marketing of minerals.**
 
 
• Its headquarter is in **New Delhi.**

GNP - Net income earned from abroad

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**GDP - Depreciation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net domestic product** (NDP) is the **total value of goods and services** produced within a country's borders, **minus the depreciation **of capital goods.
 
• **Depreciation** is the **decrease in value of an asset **over time due to wear and tear, obsolescence, or other factors.
 
• **GDP - Depreciation** is the correct answer because it** subtracts** the amount of capital goods that have been consumed or used up in the production process from the gross domestic product (GDP).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GNP - Depreciation **is incorrect because it** subtracts** the amount of capital goods used up in the production process from the** gross national product (GNP)**, which measures the total value of goods and services produced by a** country's residents,** regardless of their location.
 
• **Gross domestic product **(GDP) is the total value of goods and services produced within a **country's borders, **regardless of the nationality of the producers.
 
• **Gross national product** (GNP) is the** total value of goods and services** produced by a country's residents, regardless of their location.
 
• **Net income earned from abroad** is the **difference** between the income earned by a country's residents from **abroad **(such as from foreign investments or employment) and the income earned by **foreigners** within the country.
 
• **Depreciation** is an important factor to consider in **calculating NDP** because it reflects the **decrease **in the value of capital goods over time and the need for reinvestment in new capital goods to maintain or increase production levels.

questions.question: Which of the following claims concerning the magnetic lines of force inside a bar magnet is true?

options.text: From S-pole to N-pole of the magnet
Depends on the cross-sectional area of the bar magnet
From N-pole to S-pole of the magnet

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** From S-pole to N-pole of the magnet.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** magnetic lines of force** inside a **bar magnet** run from the **South pole** to the **North pole** of the magnet.
 
• This is because the magnetic field is oriented in such a way that it flows from the **South pole to the North pole.**
 
• The strength of the magnetic field is **greatest** at the **poles of the magnet** and **gradually decreases **as you move away from them.
 
• The orientation of the magnetic field is determined by the orientation of the **magnetic domains **within the magnet, not its shape or size.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Magnetic lines of force are also known as **magnetic field lines **or** flux lines.**
 
• They represent the direction and** strength of the magnetic field** at each point in space.
 
• The direction of the magnetic field is defined as the **direction that a compass needle** would point if placed at that point in space.
 
• The **strength** of the magnetic field is proportional to the **density **of the magnetic field lines, with more lines indicating a** stronger field.**
 
• Magnetic fields are created by the movement of **electric charges,** such as the flow of electrons in a wire or the** spinning of electrons **within atoms.

questions.question: Which of these is a component of the tertiary sector of an economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hotels and restaurants.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __ Key Points__

__
 
• **Hotels and restaurants** are a component of the** tertiary sector **of an economy.
 
• The tertiary sector is also known as the **service sector, **and it includes all activities that provide services to** consumers **and other businesses.
 
• In the** three-sector model**, the third economic sector is the** tertiary sector.**
 
• The** primary** and** secondary** sectors are the others. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mining and quarrying** is a component of the **primary sector** of an economy, which includes all activities related to natural resources extraction.
 
• **Water supply** is a component of the **utility sector** of an economy, which includes all activities related to the provision of public utilities such as water, electricity, and gas.
 
• **Electricity** is also a component of the **utility sector** of an economy, as it is a public utility that is essential for many other economic activities.
 
• All operations with the ultimate goal of using up natural resources—**agricultural, fishing, forestry, mining, and deposits**—are included in the **primary sector.**
 
• The portion of the economy centered on manufacturing is known as the** secondary sector.**
 
 
• **Construction, fabrication, assembly, distillation, and purification** are examples of secondary sector activities.

questions.question: Which Asian country was the host of the first Asian Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** India.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **first Asian Games** were held in **India** in **1951.**
 
• The event was officially called the First Asian Games, and it was held in **New Delhi.**
 
• The** Indian Olympic Association** was responsible for organizing the event.
 
• The Asian Games are now held** every four years**, and they feature athletes from all over Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thailand** hosted the Asian Games in **1966 and 1998.**
 
• **Indonesia **hosted the Asian Games in** 1962, and 2018.**
 
• **Japan** hosted the Asian Games in **1958 and 1994.**
 
• The most recent iteration of the games took place from** September 23, 2023**, to** October 8, 2023**, in **Hangzhou, China.** 
 
• With the most medals earned, **People's Republic of China **is in the lead in the medal standings. 
 
• **India **has so far taken home **107 medals**, including **28 gold **ones.

questions.question: Sleeping sickness is a vector-borne disease caused by the infection of which microscopic parasite of the species?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Trypanosoma brucei.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sleeping sickness** is caused by the microscopic parasite** Trypanosoma brucei.**
 
• The disease is transmitted to humans through the bite of **infected tsetse flies,** which are found in sub-Saharan Africa.
 
• If left untreated, sleeping sickness can cause serious **neurological damage** and eventually lead to death.
 
• Treatment involves medication that **targets the parasite, **but early diagnosis is critical as the disease becomes more difficult to treat as it progresses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Balantioides coli **is a **protozoan parasite.**

 
 
• It can infect **humans and animals.**
 
 
 
• **Giardia duodenalis** is a parasite that causes a **diarrheal illness** called giardiasis.
 
 
• These have a **pear-like form** and are between 10 and 20 micrometers long. 
 
 
 
• **Cyclospora cayetanensis** is another parasitic pathogen that can cause **diarrhea.**
 
 
• Numerous fresh vegetable varieties, such as **raspberries, mesclun and romaine lettuce, snow peas, basil, and cilantro**, have been connected to foodborne outbreaks.

questions.question: The Chari Folk dance is primarily performed by women of which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chari dance** is a popular folk dance of **Rajasthan**, which is mainly performed by women of the** Kanjar community.**
 
• It is a celebratory dance that is performed during **weddings** and other festive occasions.
 
• The word "chari" means a **pot or a vessel,** and in this dance form, the women balance **brass pots **on their heads while dancing.
 
• The pots are often lit with** cotton and ghee**, which creates a beautiful effect in the dark.
 
• The dance is accompanied by traditional **Rajasthani music**, which is played on instruments like **dholak, harmonium, and manjeera.**
 
• The dancers move in a **circular formation**, and the dance is characterized by graceful movements and twirls.
 
• Chari dance is also considered a form of worship, as it is performed to please the deity **Baba Ramdeo, **who is believed to have magical powers.
 
• The dance is often performed in his honor at his** temple** in Rajasthan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odisha** is known for its rich cultural heritage and has several traditional dance forms like **Odissi, Chhau, and Gotipua. **
 
• **Karnataka** is famous for its classical dance form, Bharatanatyam, as well as folk dances like **Yakshagana and Dollu Kunitha.**
 
• **Jharkhand** has a rich tribal culture and is known for its folk dances like** Jhumar, Paika, and Chhau.**

questions.question: In 2023, the Government of India launched the nationwide 'Sarva Dawa Sevan' or mass drug administration to eliminate the disease ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**lymphatic filariasis.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lymphatic filariasis** is a** parasitic infection** that can cause severe **swelling and disability,** known as **elephantiasis.**
 
• It is spread by mosquitoes and affects over **120 million people** worldwide, with the majority of cases in India.
 
• The **Sarva Dawa Sevan program** aims to eliminate lymphatic filariasis by** administering drugs **to entire populations in high-risk areas, regardless of whether they are infected or not.
 
• This approach is known as **mass drug administration.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thalassemia** is a **genetic blood disorder**.

 
 
• It affects the production of **hemoglobin**, which can lead to **anemia. **
 
 
 
• **Zika virus** is a mosquito-borne virus.
 
 
• It can cause **birth defects** and **neurological problems**.
 
 
 
• **Multi-drug resistant tuberculosis** (MDR-TB) is a form of tuberculosis that is resistant to the two most powerful anti-TB drugs.
 
 
• It is a** serious public health threat** in India.
